subject: MLR estimator returned NA in robust statistics

messages.author: 0571cf9b8ce66d05
messages.subject: MLR estimator returned NA in robust statistics
parts:
Hello.
I tried to use MLR estimator, but it returned NA in robust statistics.
The script is below.

df <- structure(list(x1 = c(7, 7, 4.83333, 5, 5.66667, 6.33333, 5.66667, 
6.16667, 6.83333, 6, 7, 5.66667, 5.33333, 6.83333, 6.66667, 5.83333, 
6.66667, 4.83333, 6.5, 6.33333), x2 = c(2.66667, 2.91667, 2.66667, 
2.58333, 3.41667, 3.5, 2.66667, 2.66667, 2.91667, 2.5, 2.75, 
2.58333, 3.75, 3.33333, 3.25, 2.58333, 2.91667, 2.75, 3, 2.83333
), x3 = c(314286, 3.14286, 3.85714, 3.28571, 3.14286, 4.71429, 
3.85714, 4.28571, 4.57143, 3.14286, 4.85714, 4.42857, 3.85714, 
4, 5, 4, 4.57143, 3.14286, 4.57143, 4.57143), x4 = c(NA, 3, 2.85714, 
2.14286, 3.14286, 4, 3.85714, 4.57143, 4.42857, 2.71429, 4.14286, 
4, 4.57143, 3.71429, 4.14286, 3.57143, 4.14286, 3.28571, 3.85714, 
4.28571)), .Names = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4"), row.names = c(NA, 
-20L), class = "data.frame")

model <- 'y =~ x1 + x2
          y ~  x3 + x4'
fit <- sem(model, data = df, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml")


It didn't return error but robust statistics are NA.
Result of summary(fit) is below.

> summary(fit)
lavaan (0.5-11) converged normally after  44 iterations

  Number of observations                            20

  Number of missing patterns                         2

  Estimator                                         ML      Robust
  Minimum Function Test Statistic                2.110          NA
  Degrees of freedom                                 1           1
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.146          NA
  Scaling correction factor                                     NA
    for the Yuan-Bentler correction

In case missing="listwise", It didn't return NA.
what is wrong or is it a bug?

And because of it, fitMeasures returned error in some measures
(cfi.scaled, rfi.scaled and rni.scaled, I confirmed).

> fitMeasures(fit, fit.measures = "cfi.scaled")
Error in if (t1 == 0 && t2 == 0) { : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

It's caused by NA in X2.scaled.
I believe it shouldn't return error but NA.

messages.subject: Re: MLR estimator returned NA in robust statistics
parts:
Dear 林真広 <rin...@gmail.com>

Am I right to understand your model this way?

The dataset has four observed variables: x1, x2, x3, x4
y, the latent variable, has two observed variables, first: x1, x2
Then, y ~ x3 + x4 is not correct.
Because, y is not observed variable, but is a latent one.

wishes,

Jong-Hwa

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: MLR estimator returned NA in robust statistics
parts:
On 02/20/2013 06:40 AM, 林真広 wrote:
> Hello.
> I tried to use MLR estimator, but it returned NA in robust statistics.
> The script is below.

This is an interesting example. I believe the reason for the failure is
a mistake in the data:

Note that the first element of x3 is a factor 100000 times larger than
the other elements. Presumably, it should be 3.14286 (and if you change
this, the problems go away). This outlier, combined with the small
sample size, are the reason why MLR failed.

The lesson for me is that lavaan should try and catch these anomalies
before we go on.

Yves.

I looked at the sample statistics using

inspect(fit, "sampstat")

for the model with, and the model without listwise deletion, and
observed a huge difference in the x3 row/column. Since there is only one
missing value, in the first row, it was easy to spot the outlier.

In addition,

varTable(fit)

immediately shows that the mean+var of 'x3' is huge.

Yves.
